newsitem.title: JAPAN: US Treasuries stuck in narrow ranges in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: US Treasuries stuck in narrow ranges in Tokyo.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries were stuck in narrow ranges in Tokyo trade on Thursday, amid limited activity by Tokyo traders and investors.
Some Japanese city banks showed buying interest in the five- and 10-year sectors, while insurers and pension funds unloaded short-dated issues, market sources said.
Focus is on U.S. May retail sales and jobs data due in the coming weeks, which would indicate the extent of the slowdown expected for the U.S. economy in the second quarter.
The benchmark 6-5/8 percent 30-year bond was at 94-31/32 to yield 7.03 percent, unchanged from Wednesday.
The long bond moved in a narrow 94-30/32 to 95-1/32 range.
The unwinding of so-called "yen carry trades" by hedge funds has subsided, traders said.

In yen carry trade, funds borrowed low-cost yen funds and converted them into dollars through currency and interest rate swaps. The recent surge in yen interest rates, however, made such transactions no longer profitable.
Some traders, however, said that hedge funds still need to unwind their short U.S. equities and long U.S. Treasuries positions, capping the Treasury market's advance.

On the CBOT, the key June contract was last traded at 108-24/32, up from 108-23/32 at the previous settlement. June was stuck in a narrow trading range of 108-23/32 to 108-25/32 in the overnight session.
The benchmark will shift to September on Friday.
